 India Today Video Desk UPDATED: Nov 6, 2026 07:43 IST Delhi and the National Capital Region continue to reel under severe and hazardous air quality ahead of Diwali, with average Air Quality Index levels crossing the 500 mark. Dense smog enveloped parts of Delhi and Noida, with monitoring stations in Rohini and Punjabi Bagh recording AQI readings of 473 and 464 respectively. Calm wind conditions and geography have trapped pollutants from local and external sources, rendering measures under the Winter Action Plan and Graded Response Action Plan Stage 2 inadequate on the ground. The worsening air quality has also disrupted sporting fixtures, prompting the Board of Control for Cricket in India to shift the first One Day International between India and Sri Lanka from Arun Jaitley Stadium in Delhi to Visakhapatnam. The move recalls the December 2017 Test match where visiting Sri Lankan players wore masks and experienced respiratory distress. Experts and ground reports emphasize the absence of preventive, long-term interstate planning between the Centre and states to curb the seasonal pollution crisis.

 4:16 Karnataka Ballot Paper Push Sparks Row Post MLC Poll Loss and Internal Rift 
 The Karnataka government has confirmed that upcoming local body elections will be conducted using ballot papers following cabinet approval, even as the State Election Commission decides whether to use the old or new voters list. The move comes despite the Congress suffering a 4-0 defeat against the NDA in recent MLC elections conducted via ballots. The decision has sparked internal debate within the Congress, with MP D.K. Suresh previously questioning the replacement of EVMs. Meanwhile, the BJP has strongly opposed the decision, with Union Minister Pralhad Joshi terming the shift regressive and accusing the state government of attempting to cover up its electoral setbacks.
 0:48 Vijay, Trisha, Gautam Adani & KTR Attend YS Anil Reddy's Daughter's Reception 
 Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Vijay and actor Trisha Krishnan attended the wedding reception of Y.S. Anil Reddy's daughter in Chennai on Thursday. Y.S. Anil Reddy is the cousin of former Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister and YSRCP supremo Y.S. Jaganmohan Reddy. Bharat Rashtra Samithi Working President K.T. Rama Rao, along with his wife Shalini, and Adani Group Chairman Gautam Adani were also present at the high-profile gathering.
 7:55 Dr Alia Nazneen Jukaku: 'It Is A Big Moment For Our Entire Family' 
 Speaking from Bhatkal in Karnataka, Dr. Alia Nazneen Jukaku, the aunt of Dr. Sarah Jukaku, shared her family's joy following Abdul El-Sayed's historic victory as the first Muslim senator in United States history. She noted that while her family is accustomed to local politics through her father and uncle, this victory is on a completely different level. Recalling election night, Dr. Alia mentioned that relatives across the world stayed awake monitoring news and group chats until the confirmation arrived. Addressing political attacks during the campaign, she highlighted El-Sayed's poise, remarking, 'He knew how to reply, and he was more focused on his goals.' She pointed to his door-to-door dedication and commitment to addressing public health, inflation, and healthcare affordability as key reasons for his connection with voters.
 advertisement 3:40 Democrat Abdul El-Sayed Scripts History as First Muslim Elected to US Senate 
 Democrat Abdul El-Sayed has created history in the US midterm elections by becoming the first Muslim elected to the United States Senate. The 42-year-old physician, public health expert, and son of Egyptian immigrants defeated Republican candidate Mike Rogers in Michigan. Centring his progressive campaign on healthcare reform, eliminating corporate influence, and tackling rising living costs, El-Sayed overcame sustained identity-based political attacks. His historic victory marks a major milestone for Muslim American representation in Congress.
